facts.statement: The only known species of Barapasaurus is Barapasaurus tagorei.
facts.quote: The only species is B. tagorei.

facts.statement: Barapasaurus fossils come from the lower part of the Kota Formation, dating to the Early to Middle Jurassic.
facts.quote: Barapasaurus comes from the lower part of the Kota Formation, which is of Early to Middle Jurassic in age.

facts.statement: All known Barapasaurus fossils come from a single locality near the village of Pochampally in central India.
facts.quote: All known fossils come from a single locality in the vicinity of the village of Pochampally (Pin Code: 442504), bordering Telangana (Pochampally Sironcha Taluka, Gadchiroli District, Vidarbha, Maharashtra, in central India).

facts.statement: The first Barapasaurus bones were discovered in 1958, with most specimens unearthed in 1960 and 1961.
facts.quote: The first bones were discovered in 1958, but most specimens were unearthed in 1960 and 1961.

facts.statement: Barapasaurus was scientifically described in 1975 by paleontologist Sohan Lal Jain and colleagues.
facts.quote: In 1975, the finds were described scientifically by palaeontologist Sohan Lal Jain and colleagues.

facts.statement: A more detailed osteological description of Barapasaurus was published in 2010 by Bandyopadhyay and colleagues.
facts.quote: In 2010, a more detailed osteological description was published by Bandyopadhyay and colleagues.

facts.statement: Barapasaurus fossils are archived at the Indian Statistical Institute, with most bones mounted at its Geological Museum.
facts.quote: The material is archived in the palaeontological collection of the Indian Statistical Institute (ISI), while a majority of the bones are part of a mount at the Geological Museum of the ISI.

facts.statement: The name Barapasaurus means 'big-legged lizard', derived from Indian words for 'big' and 'leg' combined with the Greek word for 'lizard'.
facts.quote: The name Barapasaurus ("big-legged lizard") is derived from bara meaning 'big' and pa meaning 'leg' in several Indian languages including Bengali; the Greek word sauros means 'lizard'.

facts.statement: The species name tagorei honors the Bengali poet Rabindranath Tagore.
facts.quote: The specific name tagorei means 'Tagore's', which honours Bengali poet, writer, painter, and musician Rabindranath Tagore.

facts.statement: Fieldwork for Barapasaurus began in the centenary year of Rabindranath Tagore's birth.
facts.quote: The first year of fieldwork was carried out in the centenary year of Tagore's birth.

facts.statement: Barapasaurus had elongated cervical vertebrae that resulted in a long neck, a trait typical of later sauropods.
facts.quote: Although a very early and unspecialised sauropod, Barapasaurus shows the building plan typical for later, more derived sauropods: the cervical vertebrae were elongated, resulting in a long neck.

facts.statement: Barapasaurus had a short trunk and columnar limbs indicating an obligate quadrupedal posture.
facts.quote: The trunk was short and holds columnar limbs which indicate an obligate quadrupedal posture.

facts.statement: Barapasaurus is estimated to be 12 to 14 meters long and weigh 7 tons, comparable to later sauropods.
facts.quote: Even the size, which is estimated at 12 to 14 m long and 7 t in weight, is comparable with that of later sauropods.

facts.statement: Barapasaurus vertebrae show early hints of hollowing in the central and neural spines as a weight-saving measure.
facts.quote: The central and neural spines show early hints of hollowing as a weight-saving measure.

facts.statement: Barapasaurus dorsal vertebrae are stabilized by hyposphene-hypantrum articulations that link the vertebrae together.
facts.quote: The dorsal vertebrae are stabilised with hyposphene-hypantrum articulations, accessory projections that link the vertebrae with each other.

facts.statement: Barapasaurus has a strengthened sacrum with an additional fourth sacral vertebra.
facts.quote: The sacrum is strengthened through an additional fourth sacral vertebra.

facts.statement: Barapasaurus teeth are spoon-shaped with wrinkled enamel and coarse serration, similar to later sauropods.
facts.quote: Like that of later sauropods, the teeth are spoon shaped and show wrinkled enamel. A basal trait is the coarse serration.

facts.statement: The presence of six left femora indicates that at least six Barapasaurus individuals were present.
facts.quote: Because there are six left femora, the total number of individuals is at least six.

facts.statement: Researchers hypothesize that water streams removed light skull bones, leaving only heavy postcranial bones, explaining the lack of skull fossils.
facts.quote: The disarticulated skull bones were removed by the water stream because they were light, leaving only the heavy postcranial bones at the site, which would explain why no skull bones were found.

facts.statement: Barapasaurus generally dates to the Early Jurassic, specifically the Sinemurian to Pliensbachian, roughly 184 to 200 million years ago.
facts.quote: The age has generally been interpreted as Early Jurassic, with the Lower Kota Formation in particular dating to the Sinemurian to Pliensbachian, roughly 184–200 million years ago.

facts.statement: Some studies argue that the Kota Formation, and thus Barapasaurus, dates to the Middle Jurassic or later.
facts.quote: However, some studies have argued that the Kota Formation dates to the Middle Jurassic or even later.

facts.statement: Barapasaurus lived during the Early Jurassic, approximately 189.6 to 176.5 million years ago during the Toarcian, in what is now the Indian subcontinent.
facts.quote: que vivió a principios del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente 189,6 y 176,5 millones de años, durante el Toarciano, en lo que hoy es el subcontinente indio.

facts.statement: When first described in 1975, Barapasaurus was not attributed to a specific group, though it showed many basal, prosauropod-like features.
facts.quote: When first described in 1975, it was not attributed to one specific group at all, although the presence of many basal, prosauropod-like features was noted.

facts.statement: From 1984, Barapasaurus was grouped with Vulcanodon in the family Vulcanodontidae, but this family was declared invalid in 1995 for being polyphyletic.
facts.quote: Since 1984, Barapasaurus was united with another early sauropod, Vulcanodon, in a family called Vulcanodontidae, although this family was declared invalid by Paul Upchurch in 1995 because it was recognised as polyphyletic.

facts.statement: Paul Upchurch classified Barapasaurus inside Eusauropoda, making it more derived than Vulcanodon, which was placed outside this clade.
facts.quote: Upchurch erected a clade named Eusauropoda that includes all known sauropods except some very basal forms. While Vulcanodon was classified outside the Eusauropoda, Barapasaurus was classified inside it, which means that Barapasaurus is more derived than Vulcanodon.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Barapasaurus is more derived than Vulcanodon (as per Upchurch) or more basal (as per Bandyopadhyay and colleagues).
facts.quote: Although Upchurch's classification was accepted by most palaeontologists, a recent study from Bandyopadhyay and colleagues came to a contrary conclusion: these palaeontologists stated that Barapasaurus was in fact more basal than Vulcanodon and removed it from Eusauropoda.

facts.statement: Barapasaurus is classified within the infraorder Sauropoda.
facts.quote: infraordo: Sauropoda

facts.statement: The genus Barapasaurus was named by Jain, Kutty, Roy-Chowdhury, and Chatterjee in 1975.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Jain, Kutty, Roy-Chowdhury & Chatterjee, 1975

facts.statement: Barapasaurus fossils are found in clay and sandstone from the lower part of the Kota Formation.
facts.quote: Barapasaurus comes from clay and sandstone that belongs to the lower part of the Kota Formation.

facts.statement: Other vertebrates living alongside Barapasaurus included the early sauropod Kotasaurus and mammals like Kotatherium, Indotherium, and Indozostrodon.
facts.quote: Other vertebrates of this part include another early sauropod, Kotasaurus, as well as the mammals Kotatherium, Indotherium and Indozostrodon.

facts.statement: Barapasaurus possessed several primitive characteristics among sauropods.
facts.quote: El barapasaurio exhibió varias características primitivas entre los saurópodos.

facts.statement: Barapasaurus was considered a general-purpose dinosaur.
facts.quote: El barapasaurio fue algo como un dinosaurio "todo-propósito".

facts.statement: Barapasaurus had a short trunk and pillar-like limbs indicating an obligate quadrupedal posture.
facts.quote: El tronco es corto y tiene extremidades como columnas que indican una postura cuadrúpeda obligada.

facts.statement: Barapasaurus is estimated to have reached a size of approximately 14 meters.
facts.quote: El tamaño, que se estima en aproximadamente 14 metros, es comparable con la de los saurópodos posteriores.

facts.statement: Only three complete teeth and three crowns are known from the Barapasaurus skull.
facts.quote: Del cráneo, solo tres dientes enteros son conocidos y tres coronas.

facts.statement: The largest known Barapasaurus tooth is 5.8 cm in height.
facts.quote: El diente más grande conocido es de 5,8 cm de altura.

facts.statement: Barapasaurus teeth were spoon-shaped and showed wrinkled enamel.
facts.quote: Los dientes tienen forma de cuchara y muestran esmalte arrugado.

facts.statement: The name Barapasaurus means 'large-legged lizard', derived from Indian words for 'large' and 'leg' combined with the Greek word for lizard.
facts.quote: El nombre Barapasaurus, "lagarto de patas grandes", se deriva del vocablo "bara" significa 'grande' y "pa" que significa 'pierna' en varios idiomas de la India combinado con la palabra "saurus" que en griego significa lagarto.

facts.statement: The specific name tagorei honors the Bengali artist Rabindranath Tagore.
facts.quote: El nombre específico tagorei significa 'de Tagore', en homor al artista Bengali Rabindranath Tagore.

facts.statement: The first fieldwork was conducted in the centennial year of Tagore's birth.
facts.quote: El primer año de trabajo de campo se llevó a cabo en el centenario año del nacimiento de Tagore.

facts.statement: The first Barapasaurus bones were found in India in 1960.

facts.statement: Six additional skeletons have been collected from the Godavari Valley in southern India.
facts.quote: Desde ello, seis esqueletos adicionales han sido recolectados del Valle de Godavari al sur de India.

facts.statement: The first bones were discovered in 1958, but most specimens were found in 1960 and 1961.

facts.statement: Approximately 300 bones were found alongside large tree trunks scattered over an area of 276 square meters.
facts.quote: Los aproximadamente 300 huesos fueron encontrados junto con grandes troncos de árboles dispersos en una superficie de 276 metros cuadrados.

facts.statement: Bandyopadhyay and colleagues interpreted the assemblage as a herd that died due to a catastrophic event, likely a flood.
facts.quote: Bandyopadhyay y sus colegas interpretaron este conjunto como una manada que murió debido a un evento catastrófico, probablemente una inundación.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest the flood could have uprooted trees and transported both trees and Barapasaurus a certain distance before decomposition began.
facts.quote: Esta inundación podría haber arrancado los árboles y se transportan ambos, árboles y Barapasaurus, una cierta distancia antes de que empezaran a descomponerse.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that disarticulated skull bones were washed away by the current because they were lighter, leaving only heavy postcranial bones behind, which explains the absence of skull bones.
facts.quote: Los huesos del cráneo desarticulados fueron retirados por la corriente de agua porque eran más ligeros, dejando sólo los huesos poscraneales pesados en el lugar, lo que explicaría por qué no se encontraron los huesos del cráneo.
